questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All Cups are Plates.

Some Plates are Saucers.

I. All Plates are Cups.

II. Some Cups are Saucers

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

All Cups are Plates.

Some Plates are Saucers.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f65a396a8d16a5564c2f681661dee0ca23419b6c717a9b35421671d6e2b05395.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All Plates are Cups → False (Given all cups are plates all plates are cups it may be possible but not definite)

II. Some Cups are Saucers → False (It is possible but not definite)

Hence, **“Neither conclusion I nor II follows****”**.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Pans are Bottles.

All Bottles are Mugs.

**Conclusions:**

I. All Mugs are Bottles.

II. Some Mugs are Pans.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Statements:

Some Pans are Bottles.

All Bottles are Mugs.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6494babbcc6d833dc8d3b9e994beafeb36ae392d5796e22bf9a473b92261698.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All Mugs are Bottles → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. Some Mugs are Pans → True (because some pans are bottles and all bottles are mugs so some mugs are also pans)

Hence, “**Only conclusion II follows**”.

questions.question: Abhay's uncle sent him some mangoes from Konkan. If he was to eat some specific number of mangoes every day, they would have lasted for 60 days. But, Abhay's cousin Rajiv came to spend the holidays with him and both of them finished the mangoes in 36 days. If Rajiv alone was to eat the mangoes, then how many days would they have lasted?
questions.solution:
Given :

1) Abhay eat mangoes in 60 days.

2) Abhay and Rajiv eat mangoes in 36 days.

**Total work = LCM of 60 days and 36 days.**

**Total work = 180**

We know that,

**Total work = efficiency × days**

Efficiency = Total work ÷ days

**The efficiency of Abhay = Total work ÷ days**

Efficiency of Abhay = 180 ÷ 60 = 3

**The efficiency of Abhay and Rajiv = Total work ÷ days**

Efficiency of Abhay and Rajiv = 180 ÷ 36 = 5

**The efficiency of Rajiv =** Efficiency of Abhay and Rajiv - Efficiency of Abhay

Efficiency of Rajiv = 5 – 3 = 2

 We know that,

Total work = efficiency × days

Days = Total work ÷ efficiency

Days = 180 ÷ 2

Days = 90

Hence, If Rajiv eats mangoes alone he takes **“90”** days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

We know that,

**Total work = LCM of 60 days and 36 days.**

**Total work = 180**

=> Total work = efficiency × days

=> Efficiency = Total work ÷ days

=> Days = Total work ÷ efficiency

Let,

The efficiency of Abhay = A

The efficiency of Rajiv = B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ae9b193701f7c4319701bc4b4417179ae7f51b2ff4c016dfab97c6c45882409.png] 

∵ Days = Total work ÷ efficiency

Days = 180 ÷ 2

Days = 90

Hence, If Rajiv eats mangoes alone he takes “90” days.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(4, 3, 35)
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5 = 3rd number**

**In **(4, 3, 35)

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5**

= (4 + 3) × 5 

= 7 × 5 

= 35 **= 3rd Number**

Now check the all options,

**Option (1) **(8, 13, 110)

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5**

= (8 + 13) × 5 

= 21 × 5 

= 105 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (2) **(6, 9, 65)

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5**

= (6 + 9) × 5 

= 15 × 5 

= 75 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (3) **(7, 12, 95)

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5**

**= (7 + 12) × 5 **

**= 19 × 5 **

**= 95 = 3rd Number**

**Option (4) **(9, 18, 153)

**(1st number + 2ⁿd number) × 5**

= (9 + 18) × 5 

= 27 × 5 

= 135 ≠** 3rd Number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"****(7, 12, 95)****".**

questions.question: In the morning prayer of a school, Chanchal was 8th from the front, while Prince was 11th from the back in the same row. If they swap their positions, Chanchal becomes 22nd from the front. What is the number of students in the row?
questions.solution:
Given:

1) Chanchal was 8th from the front, while Prince was 11th from the back in the same row.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e717fb49c0817c9ca5a00030631f2ab597468840c02ba4a3459a9285c34d982.png] 

2) If they swap their positions, Chanchal becomes 22nd from the front.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/368b184611c731fa4414320d914b459d628eb21e42443fd6a245c4eeac978c37.png] 

=> The number of students in the row = Chanchal position from the front + chancahal position from the back -1

=> The number of students in the row = 22 + 11 – 1 = 32

Hence, total **“32”** students in the row.
